title: Rent Payment
bodyText: Tenant shall pay Landlord monthly rent of {{monthly_rent}} (Monthly Rent) in advance on the due date specified in this Lease, without demand, deduction, or setoff, except as permitted by applicable law. If the due date falls on a weekend or legal holiday, rent is due on the next business day.
notes: CO added - verified this session (statute walk + full-library audit; content itself unchanged WY added 2026-08-21 (full-library cross-check pass): generic mechanics, no CO-specific statutory language or number, confirmed no conflict with WY findings from this project. | NE extended (session 2, whole-library generic-clause audit): generic mechanics, no NE-specific statutory language or number, confirmed no conflict with NE findings from this project. | MN extended (Minnesota session, whole-library audit): generic mechanics, already vetted against KS/NE's prohibited-lease-provisions statutes (the strictest bar found in this project to date) since this clause was already tagged KS;NE; no MN-specific statutory language or number identified in this session's statute walk that conflicts. No exculpatory/liability-waiver language present. | ND ADDED 2026-09-06 (ND re-audit, exhaustive generic-clause audit prompted by the checklist-to-CSV reconciliation screen). ND's ORIGINAL whole-library audit was written up in its log but largely never executed against the CSV -- ND was shipped 'complete' with 18 displayable LEASE_CLAUSE rows against 61-75 for CO/WY/KS/NE/MN. This row is generic boilerplate carrying no ND-specific statutory interaction; ND's ch. 47-16 was read in full from primary text this session and no conflict was identified. LIABILITY-LANGUAGE CHECK: North Dakota has NO enumerated prohibited-lease-provisions statute (confirmed this session -- § 47-16-02 is a maximum-term cap, and § 47-16-13.3 supplies only case-by-case unconscionability). The exculpation exposure that forced fixes to this clause family in KS and NE therefore does not arise for ND, same reasoning as the WY addendum. 5a.1 JUDGMENT: UNIFORM -- states field changed, clause TEXT unchanged, no re-review owed on existing tags. TENANCY-TYPE CAVEAT (Addendum K.2, ND finding): this clause says 'monthly rent'. ND §§ 47-16-19/20 contemplate lodgings let at a weekly rate (presumed one-week tenancy) and set three different default rent-payment regimes -- agricultural yearly, lodgings monthly, other rents quarterly. The clause is correct for a monthly tenancy and should NOT be used unmodified for a weekly or non-monthly ND tenancy. See edu-tenancy-type-notice-nd. | SD ADDED 2026-09-07 (SD re-audit, Tier A of the L.2 exhaustive generic-clause audit). SD displayed only 13 LEASE_CLAUSE rows against 60-75 for every other state; 46 generics had no SD tag and no SD override. Triaged per L.2, not bulk-extended. Tier A = boilerplate with no SD statutory interaction, or self-limiting text that defers to applicable law. S5a.1 JUDGMENT: adding a state tag changes `states` only - no bodyText, rule_type or content_type change - so no other tagged state's rendering is affected and NO propagation to other state logs is owed. State-driven, not uniform. CROSS-STATE FLAG raised from the CA pass 2026-09-19: this row says rent is payable 'without demand, DEDUCTION, OR SETOFF'. CA had to drop that language because Civ. Code s1942 gives tenants a statutory repair-and-deduct right a lease cannot waive (see rent-payment-ca). Most states have some repair-and-deduct or rent-withholding statute, so the same wording may purport to waive a non-waivable right in several of the other eight. NOT adjudicated here - each state's statute must be read before changing their text. Flagged for the cross-state review. CROSS-STATE FLAG RESOLVED BY DRAFTING 2026-09-19. The flag: 'without demand, deduction, or setoff' can purport to waive a statutory right. Adjudicated from the library's OWN verified per-state findings rather than new statute reading - ND (s47-16-13) and SD (s43-32-9) have statutory REPAIR-AND-DEDUCT; MN has court-administered RENT ESCROW under s504B.385 whose rights 'may not be waived or modified' (s504B.465); OH has escrow under s5321.07. CO, WY, KS and NE have neither repair-and-deduct nor escrow, so the language was already safe there. Fix applied: the words 'except as permitted by applicable law' added, which is protective in all eight states and required no state-specific rewrite - the same approach that let addendum-precedence absorb its CA override. CA keeps its own row (rent-payment-ca) because that one also names Civ. Code ss1941-1942 expressly. | NV: Read in full 2026-09-24 against NRS 118A (revisor text Rev. 4/15/2026, 2025 session incorporated). Applies as written. NRS 118A.210(1) rent payable without demand or notice at the agreed time and place; setoff hedge covers 118A.360/.380 deduct remedies. DEPENDENCY: {{monthly_rent}} must be the single all-in figure required by 118A.200(6) (2025) - see rent-single-figure-nv. Shutdown exception (118A.310(2)) operates by law; clause does not purport to waive it. | TX: Read in full 2026-09-25 against Tex. Prop. Code ch. 92 (full chapter, section-open; Justia 2025 host copy with per-section history lines). Applies as written. Setoff hedge covers the statutory deduct remedies (s92.0561 repair-and-deduct, s92.164/.165 security devices, s92.301 landlord-paid utility cutoff, s92.056(f)(2) deposit-for-rent on repair termination). | NJ: added 2026-09-26 (tag-first screen, instruction 26). No NJ conflict. N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(a) nonpayment ground; tenant-paid utility shut-off rent carve-out (2A:18-61.1(a)) is preserved by 'except as permitted by applicable law'. s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | FL: Applies as written (tag-first screen, instruction 26). Fla. Stat. §83.46(1): unless otherwise agreed, rent is payable without demand or notice, at the start of each period, apportionable day to day. 'Except as permitted by applicable law' preserves the §83.60(1)(b) rent-withholding defense after 7 days' written notice. s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | AZ: Applies as written. A.R.S. §33-1314(C): rent payable without demand or notice at the time and place agreed. No payment-timing statute conflicts. s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | ND 2026-09-28: the LIABILITY-LANGUAGE CHECK above is withdrawn as to any clause disclaiming liability for the landlord's own violation of law. North Dakota does have enumerated bans outside its landlord-tenant title: N.D.C.C. §§9-08-02 (exculpation), 9-08-03 (penalties), 9-08-04 (liquidated damages) and 9-08-05 (restricting enforcement). See edu-prohibited-lease-terms-nd. | GA: Applies as written (tag-first screen, instruction 26). No Georgia statute sets rent timing; O.C.G.A. § 44-7-16 makes rent bear interest from the time it is due. 'Except as permitted by applicable law' preserves any statutory setoff (none located in ch. 7). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | NC: Applies as written (tag-first screen, instruction 26). No North Carolina statute sets rent timing. The tenant may not withhold rent before a judicial determination of a right to do so (N.C. Gen. Stat. § 42-44(c)), which 'except as permitted by applicable law' already respects. Forfeiture for nonpayment when the lease has no forfeiture clause needs a demand and 10 days (N.C. Gen. Stat. § 42-3); 'without demand' in this clause is about paying rent, not about that forfeiture demand. s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | SC: Tagged. Rent is payable without demand or notice at the agreed time and place (S.C. Code Ann. § 27-40-310(c)); 'except as permitted by applicable law' preserves the tenant's essential-services procure-and-deduct remedy (S.C. Code Ann. § 27-40-630(a)(1)); South Carolina has no repair-and-deduct right (S.C. Code Ann. § 27-40-630(c)). | TN: Tagged 2026-09-28 (section text read 2026-09-28 in the built-in browser (Justia host copy of the 2025 Tennessee Code with history lines; 2025-2026 public chapters screened; TN log §1)). Tenn. Code Ann. § 66-28-201(c) (Act counties): rent payable without demand at the agreed time and place; the weekend/holiday roll is contractual and lawful everywhere. TN-SCOPE: STATEWIDE. | VA: Tagged 2026-09-28. VA-SCOPE: STATEWIDE. Read against the official Code of Virginia section-open (law.lis.virginia.gov; VA log §1). Basis: Va. Code Ann. § 55.1-1204(D): rent payable without demand or notice at the agreed time and place; the weekend/holiday roll is contractual and lawful; 'deduction or setoff, except as permitted by applicable law' preserves repair-and-deduct (Va. Code Ann. § 55.1-1244.1) and escrow (Va. Code Ann. § 55.1-1244). | AL: Tagged (applies as written). Rent is payable without demand or notice at the time and place agreed (Ala. Code § 35-9A-161(c)); 'without deduction or setoff, except as permitted by applicable law' matches the bar on withholding rent while in possession (Ala. Code § 35-9A-164). The weekend roll-forward is contractual; the Act separately rolls a statutory period ending on a weekend or holiday to the next business day (Ala. Code § 35-9A-141(3)). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | PA: Tagged. No Pennsylvania statute on rent timing; 'without ... deduction, or setoff, except as permitted by applicable law' preserves the utility deduction (66 Pa.C.S. § 1529), City Rent Withholding Act escrow (35 P.S. § 1700-1) and judge-made habitability remedies (case law, instruction 16). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | UT: 'Except as permitted by applicable law' preserves the repair-and-deduct remedy (Utah Code Ann. § 57-22-6(4)(a)(ii)). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | IL: Tagged. No Illinois statute on rent timing; 'without ... deduction, or setoff, except as permitted by applicable law' preserves repair-and-deduct (765 ILCS 742/5), landlord-paid utility deductions (765 ILCS 735/1) and radon mitigation deductions (420 ILCS 46/30(b)). Read section-open 2026-09-30 (IL log §1). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | ID: The 'except as permitted by applicable law' carve-out covers the tenant's statutory smoke-detector install-and-deduct right (Idaho Code § 6-320(a)(6)). Lawful as written. Read section-open 2026-09-30 from legislature.idaho.gov (ID log s1). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | MO: Applies as written. 'Rent' is 'a stated payment for the temporary possession or use of a house, land or other real property, made at fixed intervals' (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 441.005(5)). Read section-open 2026-09-30 (MO log §1). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | IN: Applies as written. Because the clause requires rent in advance, a landlord needs no notice to terminate for unpaid advance rent under Ind. Code § 32-31-1-8(5); default-by-tenant still requires written notice (see that row's IN note). No repair-and-deduct statute (edu-tenant-repair-remedies-in). Read section-open 2026-09-30 from iga.in.gov (IN log §1). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | OK: Okla. Stat. tit. 41, § 109(B): rent is payable at the time and place agreed. 'Except as permitted by applicable law' preserves repair-and-deduct and essential-service deductions (Okla. Stat. tit. 41, § 121(B), (C)). Weekend/holiday roll-forward is a lease term (Okla. Stat. tit. 41, § 61 excludes a legal holiday only for times set by Title 41). Read section-open 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-01 from oklegislature.gov (OK log §1). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | MI: Applies as written; 'without demand, deduction, or setoff, except as permitted by applicable law' preserves rent excused by the landlord's breach of the covenants (Mich. Comp. Laws § 600.5741) and Housing Law rent escrow (Mich. Comp. Laws § 125.530). Read section-open 2026-10-01 from legislature.mi.gov (MI log §1). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | IA: Applies as written. Iowa Code § 562A.9(3): rent payable without demand or notice at the agreed time and place. 'Except as permitted by applicable law' preserves the tenant's statutory deductions (Iowa Code §§ 562A.23(1)(a), 562A.27(4), 10A.518(7)).

title: Late Fee
bodyText: If Tenant fails to pay Monthly Rent in full within {{late_fee_grace_days}} days after it is due, a late fee of {{late_fee_amount}} will be assessed. Acceptance of a late payment does not waive Landlord's right to require full payment of Rent on the date it is due or to pursue any other remedy available under this Lease.
notes: CO added - verified this session (statute walk + full-library audit; content itself EDITED this session WY added 2026-08-21 (full-library cross-check pass): generic mechanics, no CO-specific statutory language or number, confirmed no conflict with WY findings from this project. | NE extended (session 6): the non-waiver sentence isn't prohibited in Nebraska the way the exculpation clauses were in Kansas — it's just insufficient on its own to satisfy §76-1433's after-the-breach requirement. No override needed; see edu-late-rent-reservation-fix-ne for the landlord-facing explanation of why lease text alone doesn't solve this and what actually does. | NE REMOVED 2026-08-31 (NE re-audit) — superseded by late-fee-ne. §76-1433 read verbatim from nebraskalegislature.gov. This clause's phrase 'or to pursue any other remedy available under this Lease' is UNQUALIFIED and therefore purports to preserve termination for the very breach §76-1433 says is waived. §5a.1 JUDGMENT — STATE-DRIVEN, not uniform: the fix was deliberately NOT propagated to CO, WY, or MN. A non-waiver clause preserving termination after accepting late rent is genuinely valuable where contract can preserve it, and none of those three has been shown to carry Nebraska's express statutory timing rule. Narrowing all four states would surrender real protection in three of them to solve a problem only one has. Structurally consistent with Kansas, which also took its own late-fee-ks override. | ND ADDED 2026-09-06 (ND re-audit, exhaustive generic-clause audit prompted by the checklist-to-CSV reconciliation screen). ND's ORIGINAL whole-library audit was written up in its log but largely never executed against the CSV -- ND was shipped 'complete' with 18 displayable LEASE_CLAUSE rows against 61-75 for CO/WY/KS/NE/MN. This row is generic boilerplate carrying no ND-specific statutory interaction; ND's ch. 47-16 was read in full from primary text this session and no conflict was identified. LIABILITY-LANGUAGE CHECK: North Dakota has NO enumerated prohibited-lease-provisions statute (confirmed this session -- § 47-16-02 is a maximum-term cap, and § 47-16-13.3 supplies only case-by-case unconscionability). The exculpation exposure that forced fixes to this clause family in KS and NE therefore does not arise for ND, same reasoning as the WY addendum. 5a.1 JUDGMENT: UNIFORM -- states field changed, clause TEXT unchanged, no re-review owed on existing tags. ND has NO statutory late-fee cap (confirmed: full read of ch. 47-16 contains no late-fee provision), so no figure conflict arises. Same non-outcome as WY. | SD ADDED 2026-09-07 (SD re-audit, Tier A of the L.2 exhaustive generic-clause audit). SD displayed only 13 LEASE_CLAUSE rows against 60-75 for every other state; 46 generics had no SD tag and no SD override. Triaged per L.2, not bulk-extended. Tier A = boilerplate with no SD statutory interaction, or self-limiting text that defers to applicable law. S5a.1 JUDGMENT: adding a state tag changes `states` only - no bodyText, rule_type or content_type change - so no other tagged state's rendering is affected and NO propagation to other state logs is owed. State-driven, not uniform. SD sets no statutory late-fee cap and no mandatory grace period, so the landlord-set fields create no conflict. The non-waiver sentence is also safe: SD has no waiver-by-acceptance rule of the NE S76-1433 / KS type. MATERIAL GAP CLOSED: SD previously had NO late-fee clause of any kind, and because SD law leaves late fees entirely to the lease, an SD lease generated without this clause could not charge a late fee at all. | FL: Applies as written (tag-first screen, instruction 26). No late-fee cap or grace-period statute in Fla. Stat. ch. 83 Part II (full read, §§83.40-83.684); boundary: Part II only, other titles not searched. Local fee caps are preempted by Fla. Stat. §83.425 ('fees charged by the landlord'; s. 1, ch. 2023-314). The amount stays subject to §83.45 (unconscionability). The clause does not designate the fee as rent; under §83.43(12) only payments 'designated as rent in a written rental agreement' are rent. Library default (Taylor, NJ 2026-09-26): fees are not labeled rent. s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | FL: FL research pass 2026-09-26 (advanced research, once; report in the conversation). Trial-level Florida decisions (secondary) treat a 3-day notice that demands a late charge not designated as rent as defective; the library's no-'additional rent' posture avoids that. No statewide late-fee cap found (not a full-text verified absence). | ND 2026-09-28: the LIABILITY-LANGUAGE CHECK above is withdrawn as to any clause disclaiming liability for the landlord's own violation of law. North Dakota does have enumerated bans outside its landlord-tenant title: N.D.C.C. §§9-08-02 (exculpation), 9-08-03 (penalties), 9-08-04 (liquidated damages) and 9-08-05 (restricting enforcement). See edu-prohibited-lease-terms-nd. | ND (added 2026-09-28): the absence of a cap is confirmed statewide, not only in ch. 47-16 (edu-no-late-fee-cap-nd). North Dakota's operative limit is not a cap: §9-08-03 voids contractual penalties outright and §9-08-04 voids advance-fixed damages unless actual damage would be impracticable or extremely difficult to fix. So a late fee must be defensible as an estimate of actual loss. Three cap bills have failed (2021 HB 1440, HB 1442; 2025 SB 2236). | GA: Applies as written. No Georgia late-fee cap or grace period: confirmed absent statute-wide on the official O.C.G.A. full-text search 2026-09-28 (`edu-no-fee-caps-ga`). Late fees may be demanded in the 3-business-day notice to vacate or pay (O.C.G.A. § 44-7-50(c)) and retained from the deposit (O.C.G.A. § 44-7-34(a)). The non-waiver sentence conflicts with no Georgia statute; case law on waiver by accepting late rent exists and is NOT relied on (instruction 16 flag). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | SC: Tagged. No statutory late-fee cap or grace period (confirmed absent, `edu-no-late-fee-cap-sc`); late charges are part of 'rent' (S.C. Code Ann. § 27-40-210(11)). Penalty doctrine is case law, not read. | PA: Tagged. No late-fee statute (`edu-no-late-fee-cap-pa`, confirmed absent). No statutory acceptance-waiver rule like Nebraska's and Alabama's (see `late-fee-ne`); whether accepting rent after a notice to quit waives it is case law, not read, so the base's non-waiver sentence stays. Penalty doctrine: case law. s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | UT: Utah Code Ann. § 57-22-4(5)(a) caps a late fee at the greater of 10% of the rent in the rental agreement or $75; the builder must enforce it on {{late_fee_amount}} (edu-late-fee-cap-ut). No Utah statute makes acceptance of late rent a waiver (whole-code search 17: 0 hits), so the base non-waiver sentence stays; waiver by acceptance is case law, not read. s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | IL: Tagged. No statewide Illinois late-fee cap or grace period (edu-late-fee-il). The non-waiver sentence does not conflict with the statutory partial-payment rule for 5-day notices (735 ILCS 5/9-209). The fee must also appear on page 1 (765 ILCS 705/35(b); fee-disclosure-first-page-il). Chicago's ordinance limits late fees (flag, not read). The fee law applies to leases entered into after its effective date (January 1, 2027 in official records; the Act's text says July 1, 2026; IL log §1.2). Read section-open 2026-09-30 (IL log §1). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | ID: Idaho Code § 55-305(1): any fees imposed on a residential tenant, including late fees, 'shall be reasonable'; no fixed cap, grace period or acceptance-waiver statute (whole-code search). Under a written agreement entered into or renewed on or after July 1, 2023, the late fee may not exceed the amount agreed and must be stated in the agreement or added on 30 days' written notice (Idaho Code § 55-305(2)-(3)). See edu-late-fee-reasonable-id. The base non-waiver sentence stays (no Idaho acceptance-waiver statute; case law not read). Read section-open 2026-09-30 from legislature.idaho.gov (ID log s1). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | MO: Applies as written. No Missouri late-fee cap or grace period (whole-code search, MO battery 10: 36 sections, none a residential-lease rule; edu-no-late-fee-cap-mo). No acceptance-waiver statute; whether accepting late rent waives strict compliance is case law, not read (the revisor's annotation to Mo. Rev. Stat. § 534.330 reports Fritts v. Cloud Oak Flooring Co. (Mo. App. 1972) on this point; not read). The penalty doctrine is case law, not read. Read section-open 2026-09-30 (MO log §1). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | IN: Applies as written. No Indiana late-fee cap or grace period (IN battery 10: 36 sections, none a residential-lease rule; edu-no-late-fee-cap-in). No acceptance-waiver statute (IN battery 96); case law not read. Local regulation of landlord fees is preempted (Ind. Code § 32-31-1-20(c)(7)). Read section-open 2026-09-30 from iga.in.gov (IN log §1). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | OK: No Oklahoma statute caps or regulates residential late fees (OK batteries 19/27/29 and Title 41 read whole). Contract doctrine applies: a penalty for non-performance is void (Okla. Stat. tit. 15, §§ 213, 214) and a stipulated amount is valid only where 'from the nature of the case, it would be impracticable or extremely difficult to fix the actual damage' (Okla. Stat. tit. 15, § 215(A); the real-estate-sales exception in Okla. Stat. tit. 15, § 215(B) does not reach leases); damages must be reasonable (Okla. Stat. tit. 23, § 97). The Oklahoma Real Estate Commission's 2026 Residential Lease states its late fee as liquidated damages (OK log §15). A lease-required fee is 'rent' by definition (Okla. Stat. tit. 41, § 102(11)); whether a late fee supports a five-day nonpayment notice and how Oklahoma courts apply Okla. Stat. tit. 15, § 215 to late fees is unread case law (edu-fees-as-rent-ok, edu-penalties-liquidated-damages-ok). Read section-open 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-01 from oklegislature.gov (OK log §1). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | MI: Applies as written; no Michigan statute caps or regulates residential late fees (MI battery 13: 12 hits, none residential). Penalty test: Michigan courts enforce an agreed sum that is reasonable with relation to the possible injury suffered and not unconscionable or excessive, and decide enforceability as a question of law (Curran v Williams, 352 Mich 278, 282 (1958); UAW-GM Human Resource Ctr v KSL Recreation Corp, 228 Mich App 486, 508 (1998)); no published Michigan case applying the test to a residential lease fee was found (MI log §1.4). Read section-open 2026-10-01 from legislature.mi.gov (MI log §1). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | MN extended (Minnesota session, whole-library audit): generic non-waiver mechanics compatible with Minn. Stat. § 504B.177(a) — statute requires the written agreement to specify when the fee is imposed, which the {{late_fee_grace_days}} mechanic satisfies. Paired with late-fee-limit-mn for the 8% cap. | MN (retro checks, SOP 1.19, 2026-10-02; a scalpel, not a re-audit): ITEM 18 / RULE 78 -- DANGLING POINTER REPOINTED IN THE MN SEGMENT ONLY. The MN note said 'Paired with late-fee-limit-mn for the 8% cap'; the 2026-09-29 scrub switched that row off, leaving the pointer dead and, worse, leaving Minnesota with no statement of the Minn. Stat. Sec. 504B.177 cap anywhere. `late-fee-limit-mn` has been restored and rewritten in this pass to carry the 8% ceiling, the written-agreement-specifying-when condition and the housing-assistance subsidy-portion rule, so the pairing is live again. Sec. 504B.177 read section-open this pass; the {{late_fee_grace_days}} mechanic still satisfies the statute's requirement that the agreement specify when the fee is imposed. Sec. 5a.1 / rule 62: this is a NOTES-ONLY change inside the MN segment -- bodyText, rule_type, content_type and states are untouched, so no other tagged state is affected and no propagation is owed.

title: Returned Checks / Dishonored Payments
bodyText: If any payment of Rent is returned for insufficient funds or otherwise fails, Landlord may require that the payment be replaced by a cashier's check, certified check, or money order, and may charge Tenant a fee associated with the failed payment, not to exceed the maximum amount permitted by applicable law. If more than two of Tenant's payments during the Term are returned for insufficient funds, Landlord may require all future payments of Rent be made by cashier's check, certified check, or money order.
notes: CO added - verified this session (statute walk + full-library audit; content itself unchanged WY added 2026-08-21 (full-library cross-check pass): generic mechanics, no CO-specific statutory language or number, confirmed no conflict with WY findings from this project. | NE extended (session 2, whole-library generic-clause audit): generic mechanics, no NE-specific statutory language or number, confirmed no conflict with NE findings from this project. | MN extended (Minnesota session, whole-library audit): generic mechanics, already vetted against KS/NE's prohibited-lease-provisions statutes (the strictest bar found in this project to date) since this clause was already tagged KS;NE; no MN-specific statutory language or number identified in this session's statute walk that conflicts. No exculpatory/liability-waiver language present. | ND extended (North Dakota session 1): confirmed via enacted text of N.D.C.C. § 47-16-20.1 (provided directly by Taylor) that ND's 2025 payment-fee statute governs a different topic (fee for accepting cash/check/money order as a payment method) than returned/NSF payment fees. No conflict with this clause's generic mechanics; the actual NSF cap lives in Title 6 general banking law (§6-08-16), not landlord-tenant law, and isn't restated here. | KS CHECKED 2026-08-30 (v59 canvass): K.S.A. 60-2610(g) caps the service charge on a dishonored check at $30. This clause's unqualified 'any fee associated with the failed payment' was flagged as a possible conflict, since unlike landlords-access and holdover it carries NO self-limiting 'to the extent permitted by applicable law' language. TAYLOR'S DECISION: leave as is, no KS override. Reasoning: 60-2610(g) caps the charge the drawee/vendor imposes, and under this clause the landlord recovers that charge as a pass-through loss rather than setting its own fee, so the effective ceiling is $30 either way. See edu-nsf-fee-cap-ks. | Also confirmed for KS: no payment-method fee ban (no analog to N.D.C.C. 47-16-20.1); Kansas does not restrict charging for particular payment methods. | MN re-audit 2026-09-03: MN's returned-check fee cap identified (Minn. Stat. §604.113, $30 service charge) — see edu-returned-check-fee-cap-mn. NO CLAUSE EDIT MADE and no MN override created: this clause does not hardcode a dollar figure, so it does not conflict with the cap, matching the disposition WY reached for the same situation. §5a.1 JUDGMENT: the finding is STATE-DRIVEN (each state's bad-check statute differs — WY $30, MN $30, KS/NE/ND/SD各 their own), but requires no shared-clause change because the clause is figure-agnostic. Flagged instead: the clause's phrase 'may charge Tenant any fee associated with the failed payment' is unbounded on its face and could read as authorizing more than the statutory cap in every tagged state. NOT edited here — it is tagged CO;WY;KS;NE;MN;ND and a rewording triggers §5a.1 across six states. Recommend a scoped shared-clause pass. | SHARED-CLAUSE PASS 2026-09-03 (§5a.1). EDIT: 'may charge Tenant any fee associated with the failed payment' → 'a fee ... not to exceed the maximum amount permitted by applicable law.' §5a.1 JUDGMENT: **UNIFORM** — the self-limiting formulation is correct in every tagged state regardless of each state's specific figure; safe to inherit, no per-state override needed. TRIGGER: every one of the six tagged states has a cap and a row recording it (CO nsf-fee-limit-co (switched off 2026-09-29); WY edu-returned-check-fee-cap-wy; KS edu-nsf-fee-cap-ks; NE edu-bad-check-restitution-vs-nsf-fee-ne; ND edu-returned-check-fee-cap-nd; MN edu-returned-check-fee-cap-mn, $30 under §604.113). The unbounded word 'any' was therefore wrong in all six simultaneously — a clause that promised landlords something no tagged state allows. | SD ADDED 2026-09-07 (SD re-audit, Tier A of the L.2 exhaustive generic-clause audit). The clause that deferred held; the education row that hardcoded broke. | OH: no statutory cap. §1319.16's $30-or-10% ceiling binds a COLLECTION AGENCY (§1319.12(A)(2) excludes a landlord collecting its own account) and does not apply. 'Maximum permitted by applicable law' therefore resolves to no cap — state an actual amount. §5321.14 unconscionability is the only ceiling. | AZ: Applies as written. The "maximum permitted" referent exists: A.R.S. §44-6852 lets the holder of a dishonored check, draft, order or note charge a service fee of not more than $25 plus the actual charges its financial institution assessed. Civil remedy for intent to defraud: A.R.S. §12-671 (edu-dishonored-payment-remedies-az). Code Ann. § 34-11-70(a)(3)), with no statute for failed electronic or card payments. SC now uses `returned-payments-sc` (stated fee with the statutory figure shown), the pattern of `returned-payments-tn` and `returned-payments-al`. Text unchanged; states-only change, no propagation owed. | TN: Removed 2026-09-30 (SOP 1.4 retro, rule 53): the clause states only a ceiling ('the maximum amount permitted by applicable law'); Tennessee's figure is a $30 handling charge for a dishonored check, draft or order (Tenn. Code Ann. § 47-29-102). Superseded for TN by returned-payments-tn. TN-SCOPE: STATEWIDE. | AL: removed 2026-09-30 (AL retro, SOP 1.8 rule 53): the clause states only a ceiling ("not to exceed the maximum amount permitted by applicable law"). Alabama's figure (Ala. Code § 8-8-15: the greater of $30 or the bank's actual return charge, for lenders, creditors and merchants, checks and like instruments only) may not reach landlords at all, leaving the ceiling with no referent. AL now uses `returned-payments-al` (stated fee with the statutory figure shown), the pattern of `returned-payments-tn`, `returned-payments-ut`, `returned-payments-il` and `returned-payments-id`. Text unchanged; states-only change, no propagation owed. | PA: Tagged. No civil returned-payment fee cap; 18 Pa.C.S. § 4105(e)(3) ($50 or bank fees) is criminal restitution only; `nsf-fee-limit-pa` rewritten as education. 'Maximum amount permitted' is safe. s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | NC: Applies as written. A payee who accepts a check may charge a processing fee of up to $35 for a check refused for insufficient funds or no account (N.C. Gen. Stat. § 25-3-506), so 'not to exceed the maximum amount permitted by applicable law' has a referent for checks. No statute located for a fee on a failed ACH or card payment (full-text search of the General Statutes 2026-09-28), so for those the clause limits nothing and the fee is contractual. Civil remedy for a knowingly bad check: N.C. Gen. Stat. § 6-21.3 (see edu-dishonored-payment-remedies-nc). K.3 check: the clause states no figure. s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | NC: REMOVED 2026-10-02 (SOP 1.21 retro, rule 53): the clause states only a ceiling, and North Carolina's $35 processing fee (N.C. Gen. Stat. § 25-3-506) reaches checks taken 'in payment for goods or services', which may not include rent, leaving the ceiling with no clear referent. NC now uses `returned-payments-nc`. Fix 24 (AZ's 'during any 12-month period'): lawful in North Carolina (no statute speaks to it); NC's override already uses it. Not a re-audit. s5a.1: states-only change.

title: Amounts Due Upfront
bodyText: Tenant will pay Landlord the following amounts, at the time specified for each: [specify what is due and when here, e.g. first month's Monthly Rent ({{monthly_rent}}) due at signing; Security Deposit ({{security_deposit}}) due at signing; Pet Deposit ({{pet_deposit}}) due at signing; last month's Monthly Rent due on the Start Date]. These amounts are due in addition to, and are not credited against, Rent due for any other month of the Term.

S5a.1 JUDGMENT: adding a state tag changes `states` only - no bodyText, rule_type or content_type change - so no other tagged state's rendering is affected and NO propagation to other state logs is owed. State-driven, not uniform. | OH: §5321.01(E) defines a security deposit as ANY deposit of money or property to secure performance — prepaid last month's rent likely falls inside §5321.16 (interest under (A), return/itemisation under (B)). Interpretive; flagged. | NV: Read in full 2026-09-24 against NRS 118A (revisor text Rev. 4/15/2026, 2025 session incorporated). Applies as written. Any prepaid last month's rent and any pet or cleaning deposit count toward the 3-months'-rent cap on total security (118A.242(1), 118A.240) - cap stated in security-deposit-cap-nv. | TX: Read in full 2026-09-25 against Tex. Prop. Code ch. 92 (full chapter, section-open; Justia 2025 host copy with per-section history lines). Applies as written. s92.102 excludes advance rent and rental-application deposits from 'security deposit'; clause keeps them distinct. No deposit cap in Subch. C. | NJ: added 2026-09-26 (tag-first screen, instruction 26). Applies as written. Deposit cap is N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 (1.5x monthly rent) - see security-deposit-return-nj; the builder should warn if {{security_deposit}} exceeds 1.5x {{monthly_rent}}. s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | FL: Applies as written (tag-first screen, instruction 26). Last month's Rent collected at signing is 'advance rent' (Fla. Stat. §83.43(2)) and must be held and disclosed under §83.49 like the deposit: see security-deposit-return-fl and security-deposit-notice-fl. s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | ND 2026-09-28: the LIABILITY-LANGUAGE CHECK above is withdrawn as to any clause disclaiming liability for the landlord's own violation of law. North Dakota does have enumerated bans outside its landlord-tenant title: N.D.C.C. §§9-08-02 (exculpation), 9-08-03 (penalties), 9-08-04 (liquidated damages) and 9-08-05 (restricting enforcement). See edu-prohibited-lease-terms-nd. | SC: Tagged. No deposit cap (confirmed absent, `edu-no-deposit-cap-sc`). Prepaid rent must be returned with the deposit notice or the tenant may recover three times the amount wrongfully withheld (S.C. Code Ann. § 27-40-410(a); S.C. Code Ann. § 27-40-410(b)); `security-deposit-return-sc` covers it. Anticipated rent paid more than 12 months ahead is not a valid discount against third persons (S.C. Code Ann. § 27-39-20). | TN: Tagged 2026-09-28 (section text read 2026-09-28 in the built-in browser (Justia host copy of the 2025 Tennessee Code with history lines; 2025-2026 public chapters screened; TN log §1)). No Tennessee statute limits amounts due at signing; no deposit cap (edu-no-deposit-cap-tn). TN-SCOPE: STATEWIDE. | VA: Tagged 2026-09-28. VA-SCOPE: STATEWIDE. Read against the official Code of Virginia section-open (law.lis.virginia.gov; VA log §1). Basis: No Virginia statute limits what is due at signing beyond the two-month deposit cap (Va. Code Ann. §§ 55.1-1226(A), 55.1-1206(C)); rent paid more than one month in advance must be escrowed (Va. Code Ann. § 55.1-1205). Does NOT satisfy the first-page fee disclosure (Va. Code Ann. § 55.1-1204.1) - that is fee-disclosure-statement-va (REQUIRED). | AL: Tagged. The security cap (one month's periodic rent, with pet, alteration and liability-risk exceptions) is in `security-deposit-cap-al` (Ala. Code § 35-9A-201(a)); prepaid rent is not security for the cap. s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | PA: Tagged. No statute on move-in payments; last month's rent collected in advance may be argued to count toward the 68 P.S. § 250.511a (Act § 511.1) cap (case law, not read) - `edu-security-deposit-rules-pa`. s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | UT: Any deposit 'however denominated' falls under Utah Code Ann. Title 57, Chapter 17 (Utah Code Ann. § 57-17-1); if there is a written agreement, a nonrefundable part must be stated in writing when the deposit is taken (Utah Code Ann. § 57-17-2; nonrefundable-deposit-notice-ut). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | IL: Tagged. Any non-optional fee listed here must also appear on page 1 (765 ILCS 705/35(b)); a banned fee (765 ILCS 705/35(c)) may not be listed. The fee law applies to leases entered into after its effective date (January 1, 2027 in official records; the Act's text says July 1, 2026; IL log §1.2). Read section-open 2026-09-30 (IL log §1). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | ID: Idaho Code § 6-321(1): any amount deposited for a purpose other than the payment of rent is a security deposit. Prepaid rent listed here is rent; a pet deposit or other deposit listed here is a refundable security deposit under Idaho Code § 6-321. Read section-open 2026-09-30 from legislature.idaho.gov (ID log s1). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | MO: Applies as written. Missouri caps security deposits at two months' rent and defines a security deposit as any deposit 'however denominated' that secures performance (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 535.300(1), (8)); whether a prepaid last month's Rent named in the bracket counts toward the cap is case law, not read (edu-deposit-last-month-mo). A pet deposit is outside the definition. Read section-open 2026-09-30 (MO log §1). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | IN: Applies as written. A required prepayment of rent other than the first full rental period is a security deposit under Indiana law (Ind. Code § 32-31-3-9(b)(1)), so last month's rent collected at signing is held, used and returned as a deposit (edu-deposit-last-month-in). Read section-open 2026-09-30 from iga.in.gov (IN log §1). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | AZ: Applies as written, with a builder caution. A.R.S. §33-1321(A) caps security "however denominated, including prepaid rent" at 1.5 months' rent (tenant may voluntarily prepay more). The bracket example lists last month's Rent due on the Start Date: prepaid last-month Rent counts toward the cap, so Security Deposit plus prepaid last-month Rent plus any refundable pet deposit must not exceed 1.5 months' Rent unless the tenant volunteers it. Cap stated in edu-security-deposit-az (security-deposit-cap-az switched off 2026-09-29; repointed 2026-09-30, AZ retro). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | OK: No Oklahoma limit on amounts due at signing; money required as returnable security is a 'deposit' held under Okla. Stat. tit. 41, § 115 (Okla. Stat. tit. 41, § 102(2)); prepaid rent must be returned when the act requires (Okla. Stat. tit. 41, §§ 115(E), 120(A), 122(B), 123). Read section-open 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-01 from oklegislature.gov (OK log §1). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | GA: Applies as written, WITH A BUILDER CAUTION. Under O.C.G.A. § 44-7-30(3) a 'security deposit' includes 'advance rent deposits' and pet deposits but excludes money 'to be applied toward the payment of rent'. Money labelled a last-month deposit is therefore inside the two-month cap (O.C.G.A. § 44-7-30.1), the escrow rule (O.C.G.A. § 44-7-31) and the return rules; prepaid rent for a named period is not. Taylor decision 2026-09-28 (GA log §6.1): money paid in advance toward the last month is treated as an advance rent deposit unless the lease expressly makes it Rent for a named calendar month (`edu-security-deposit-rules-ga`; `security-deposit-cap-ga` switched off 2026-09-29; repointed 2026-10-01, GA retro). Nonrefundable fees are outside (O.C.G.A. § 44-7-30(1), (3)). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | MI: Applies as written, with one point for the builder: in Michigan any required prepayment of rent other than the first full rental period is a security deposit (Mich. Comp. Laws § 554.601(d)), so last month's rent collected at signing counts toward the 1 1/2-month cap and the deposit rules (edu-prepaid-rent-deposit-mi). Read section-open 2026-10-01 from legislature.mi.gov (MI log §1). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | IA: Applies as written. Last month's rent paid at signing is prepaid rent, not a rental deposit (Iowa Code § 562A.6(12)), so it does not count toward the two-month deposit cap (Iowa Code § 562A.12(1)); a pet deposit does count (`edu-pet-deposit-ia`). | NC: Applies as written. North Carolina caps security deposits by tenancy type (N.C. Gen. Stat. § 42-51(b); edu-security-deposit-rules-nc). A refundable pet deposit is a security deposit and counts toward the cap; a 'reasonable, nonrefundable fee for pets' is allowed separately (N.C. Gen. Stat. § 42-53). The Tenant Security Deposit Act does not define 'security deposit' and says nothing about prepaid last-month rent, so whether the example 'last month's Monthly Rent' is a deposit is not settled by statute. Taylor decision 2026-09-28 (NC log §6, decision 1): it counts toward the cap unless the lease makes it Rent for a named calendar month (`edu-security-deposit-rules-nc`; the decision was recorded on `security-deposit-cap-nc`, switched off 2026-09-29). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | NC: RETRO 2026-10-02 (SOP 1.21, fix 20): coverage pointers repointed from the switched-off `security-deposit-cap-nc` to `edu-security-deposit-rules-nc`, which now states the tenancy-type caps and the prepaid last-month rent rule. Notes only.

title: Application of Payments
bodyText: Each payment Tenant makes will be applied first to the Monthly Rent due for the current or oldest unpaid rental period, and only then to any other fees, charges, or amounts due under this Lease, unless Tenant directs otherwise in writing for a particular payment or applicable law requires otherwise. Nothing in this provision limits any statutory right Tenant may have to cure nonpayment of Rent.

INERT in SD, not false - it saves a right that does not exist rather than asserting one does. It doesn't in every tagged state -- Ohio has no statutory right to cure nonpayment (R.C. 1923.04 is a notice to leave, not a pay-or-quit), and CO's own citation note had already separately flagged that South Dakota lacks one too ('references a tenant cure right SD does not have') without the sentence ever being fixed. Softened to 'any statutory right Tenant may have' -- self-limiting, same pattern as `holdover`'s 'maximum amount permitted by applicable law' fix -- so the sentence is accurate everywhere regardless of whether a given state has such a right, with no state-specific override needed. Uniform fix, not state-driven; applies to all 8 tagged states equally and needs no per-state re-verification, since it only removes an assertion, adding no new claim. CA: extended to California 2026-09-19 after re-screen against the full CA pass (the extend manifest had deferred tagging until the blocked set was resolved, and the step was then missed). Code s1954.07(g)(2) bars applying any amount tendered toward rent to the RENT-REPORTING FEE. The payment engine must exclude that fee from fees-first allocation. Also: a CA three-day notice may demand only RENT (CCP s1161(2)), so fees-first allocation must never be used to manufacture a rent default. | NV: Read in full 2026-09-24 against NRS 118A (revisor text Rev. 4/15/2026, 2025 session incorporated). Applies as written on its hedge. PROVISIONAL: NRS Ch. 40 summary-eviction provisions (pay-or-quit mechanics) not yet read; re-check when supplied. Note NV defines rent to include late fees (118A.150). | NV (text batch 2, 2026-09-24): PROVISIONAL CLEARED. NRS 40.253(11): after a pay-or-quit notice the landlord may not refuse rent because collection fees, attorney's fees, other non-rent costs, a reasonable late or dishonored-check charge, or a deposit are unpaid. A fees-first allocation that left the rent itself unpaid would collide with that; the row's own sentence preserving the tenant's statutory right to cure nonpayment of rent is what keeps it lawful in NV - do not remove it. | TX: Read in full 2026-09-25 against Tex. Self-limit covers s92.008(p) (payment made to avoid/restore submetered electric interruption may not be applied to rent or other amounts). Ch. 24 (eviction) not yet read. | PAYMENT ORDER CHANGED 2026-09-26 (Taylor's decision, Claude Code sync of the FL pass): fees-first replaced by rent-first for every tagged state; NJ and FL folded back in and application-of-payments-nj (switched off 2026-09-29) retired. Reason: fees-first turns an unpaid fee into an apparent rent shortfall, the number a landlord carries onto a demand notice. No tagged state's research found a statute requiring fees-first, and several found rent-only demand rules it collides with (CO C.R.S. 38-12-105, a late fee is not rent; CA CCP s1161(2); NV NRS 40.253(11); NJ Harris; FL s83.43(12)/s83.56(3)). Rent-first is lawful on any reading. Text is the NJ row's wording plus the base's 'or applicable law requires otherwise' hedge, kept because TX s92.008(p) and CA Civ. Code s1954.07(g)(2) depend on it; the cure-preserving sentence stays (NV). UNIFORM change: propagation notes appended to every tagged state's log. Rent Tracker changed to rent-first the same day. | AZ: Applies as written. Rent-first is safe in Arizona: A.R.S. §33-1368(B) reinstatement turns on past-due rent (and before filing a reasonable late fee set forth in a written lease); fees applied first could make paid rent look unpaid. s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | ND 2026-09-28: the LIABILITY-LANGUAGE CHECK above is withdrawn as to any clause disclaiming liability for the landlord's own violation of law. North Dakota does have enumerated bans outside its landlord-tenant title: N.D.C.C. §§9-08-02 (exculpation), 9-08-03 (penalties), 9-08-04 (liquidated damages) and 9-08-05 (restricting enforcement). See edu-prohibited-lease-terms-nd. | GA: Applies as written (rent first). No Georgia statute on the order of applying payments (not located; ch. 7 read whole). The cure sentence preserves the O.C.G.A. § 44-7-52 tender defense (all rent plus warrant costs within 7 days of service, once per 12 months). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | NC: Applies as written. N.C. Gen. Stat. § 42-26(b): any payment to the landlord is applied first to rent owed and then to landlord-billed water, sewer or electric charges, unless the tenant designates otherwise. The clause applies payments to rent first, honours a tenant's written direction, and yields where 'applicable law requires otherwise'. The same subsection bars using unpaid water, sewer or electric charges as a ground to terminate the lease (utility-billing-nc). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | SC: Tagged. No statute on application of payments; late charges are 'rent' (S.C. Code Ann. § 27-40-210(11)), so rent-first ordering is lawful. | TN: Tagged 2026-09-28 (section text read 2026-09-28 in the built-in browser (Justia host copy of the 2025 Tennessee Code with history lines; 2025-2026 public chapters screened; TN log §1)). 'Rents' means all payments to be made to the landlord under the rental agreement (Tenn. Code Ann. § 66-28-104(13)); rent-first ordering is lawful and leaves the § 66-28-201(d) grace period untouched. TN-SCOPE: STATEWIDE. | VA: Tagged 2026-09-28. VA-SCOPE: STATEWIDE. Read against the official Code of Virginia section-open (law.lis.virginia.gov; VA log §1). Basis: No Virginia payment-application statute; 'Rent' means all money other than a security deposit owed under the lease (Va. Code Ann. § 55.1-1200); rent-first ordering is lawful. Form 200 (Rev. 07/23) § 3(a) applies deposits to fees first - library default kept (VA log §15). | AL: Tagged. No Alabama payment-order statute located (Chapter 9A read whole). 'Rent' means all payments to or for the landlord under the rental agreement (Ala. Code § 35-9A-141(12)), so rent-first ordering is a contract choice. s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | PA: Tagged. No statutory order of application; rent-first is consistent with 68 P.S. § 250.501(b) (Act § 501(b)) and 68 P.S. § 250.503(c) (Act § 503(c): paying 'the rent actually in arrears and the costs' supersedes the writ). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | UT: No rule on applying payments in the chapters read whole (Title 57 Chapters 17 and 22, Title 78B Chapter 6 Part 8); no separate whole-code search was run; library default kept. The Utah lease used for gap-discovery source 2 applies payments to fees first (UT log s15). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | IL: Tagged. No Illinois statute sets the order in which a tenant's payment is applied (none located in the Acts read whole). Rent-first is the library default. Read section-open 2026-09-30 (IL log §1). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | ID: No Idaho statute sets an order of applying payments (whole-code search). Lawful as written. Read section-open 2026-09-30 from legislature.idaho.gov (ID log s1). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | MO: Applies as written. ITEM 19 / RULE 78 FINDING, AND IT IS WORSE THAN THE NEW JERSEY CASE THE RULE WAS WRITTEN FROM. *** The 2026-09-29 three-bucket scrub switched this row off and created NO education counterpart, so Minnesota was left with no statement of Minn. Stat. Sec. 504B.177 anywhere -- not in a clause, not in education. Every other capped state carries one (CO `edu-late-fee-limit-co`, UT `edu-late-fee-cap-ut`, NV, NJ, TN, VA, NC, TX, KS, NE, AZ all have a clause or an education row). The shared `late-fee` row supplies a free-text {{late_fee_amount}}, so after the scrub a Minnesota landlord could enter any figure with nothing in the lease or the library saying 8%. The scrub's own verdict table does not list this row at all, although it covers 'all 27 lease clauses written for this state alone' -- so the switch-off was never given a recorded verdict. WHY IT GOES BACK IN THE CLAUSE RATHER THAN EDUCATION (item 19's test): Sec. 504B.177, read section-open in full, has three limbs and two of them are conditions a number check cannot catch. (a) No late fee at all is permitted 'unless the tenant and landlord have agreed in writing that a late fee may be imposed', and 'the agreement must specify when the late fee will be imposed' -- the lease IS that writing, so the condition can only live in the lease; the {{late_fee_grace_days}} mechanic in `late-fee` supplies the 'when'. (c) A landlord under a housing assistance payments contract (42 U.S.C. 1437f or 1485, or any programme where the landlord takes rent from the tenant and a payment from government) must calculate and assess the fee ONLY on the tenant's portion of rent -- a change to the base, keyed to a tenant class, which no cap check would detect. This is the direct analogue of the N.J.S.A. 2A:42-6.1 senior and benefit-recipient grace period that New Jersey restored to `late-fee-nj`. The 8% ceiling itself is the limb a builder check could catch (backlog M.13) and is stated here anyway because the row already existed. ALSO IN THE STATUTE, NOT PUT IN THE CLAUSE: (b) where a federal statute, regulation or handbook permitting late fees for a federally subsidised tenancy conflicts with (a), the landlord may publish and implement a federally compliant fee schedule -- an override that operates outside the lease; and the definitional point that 'due date' excludes an earlier date by which paying earns the tenant a discount. Both recorded here, not drafted, because neither is a term the lease should state. A late fee is expressly 'not considered to be either interest or liquidated damages'. Currency: Sec. 504B.177 amended 2024 c 118 s 13; history line read. Rule 76: the decision to restore to the clause rather than education is a drafting judgment, made here and recorded. title: Late Fee Guidance
bodyText: Landlord and Tenant agree that if Tenant fails to pay rent when due, the actual damage to Landlord from that late payment would, from the nature of the case, be impracticable or extremely difficult to fix. Landlord and Tenant therefore agree that {{late_fee_amount}} shall be presumed to be the amount of damage sustained by Landlord from a late payment of rent. This amount is a presumed measure of Landlord's actual damages and is not a penalty.
notes: CA: REWRITTEN 2026-09-19 against Civ. Code s1671 (primary text supplied by Taylor). CONFIRMED STANDARD INVERSION - the prior dormant row recited the s1671(b) test ('a reasonable estimate of Landlord's actual damages'), which is the wrong test for a residential lease. s1671(c)(2) routes a lease of real property for use as a dwelling to subdivision (d), NOT (b). Under s1671(d) a liquidated-damages provision is VOID, except that the parties may agree on an amount presumed to be the damage 'when, from the nature of the case, it would be impracticable or extremely difficult to fix the actual damage.' Two consequences the old text got backwards: (1) the default is voidness, not validity; (2) the burden flips - under (b) the party attacking the clause must prove it unreasonable, while under (d) the landlord must bring the clause within the exception. The new body text is drafted to track (d)'s exception language rather than the (b) standard. s1671(a) yields to any other statute expressly prescribing a liquidated-damages rule for the contract - none found for residential late fees in the sections read, but note s1950.5 expressly governs security, so deposit-forfeiture provisions route there and not through s1671. NOT CONFIRMED: the old row's assertion that 'California does not set a statutory cap on late fees' is consistent with everything read this pass but is NOT a full-chapter proof-of-absence - no dedicated late-fee cap search was run. Do not upgrade that limb to CITED without one. Also unread: Orozco v. Casimiro and Del Monte Properties v. Dolan are the cases usually cited for applying s1671(d) to residential late fees; both are pointers only, neither has been read. EXTEND SCREEN 2026-09-19: now supersedes the base row `late-fee`, which is blocked for CA. s1951.5 RESOLVED 2026-09-19 (primary text supplied): it reads in its entirety 'Section 1671, relating to liquidated damages, applies to a lease of real property.' CONFIRMATORY, NOT CORRECTIVE, as predicted - s1671(c)(2) already reached a lease of real property for use as a dwelling on its own terms, and s1951.5 removes any argument that s1671 is confined to contracts for goods and services. No change to this row's analysis; the earlier flag is cleared. MILITARY TENANTS, added 2026-09-19: Mil. & Vet. Code s403(b) - no fine or penalty accrues during a court stay of an action to enforce the lease, and a court may relieve a service member from a late fee incurred while in service if military service materially impaired their ability to pay. Applies during service and within 120 days after. See edu-military-default-judgment-ca. || OPEN ITEM CLOSED 2026-09-28, gap-discovery source 4 (outside-title search). This row's notes said the 'California does not set a statutory cap on late fees' limb was NOT a proof of absence and must not be upgraded without a dedicated late-fee cap search. That search has now been run on the official leginfo code full-text search: 'late fee' in the Civil Code returns 13 sections and 'late charge' 23. Reviewed by section and title, the hits are common interest development assessments (ss5650, 5655, 5658, 5665, 5685, 5720, 6808, 6812), mortgage and deed-of-trust late charges (ss2954.4, 2954.5), retail installment and consumer credit (ss1812.402, 1812.626, 1812.643, 1799.91), debt collection (s1788.102), s3273.23, and the WATER SUBMETER sections. NO general cap on residential rent late fees exists, so the s1671(d) analysis in this row is the whole of the law on the amount. ONE REAL EXCEPTION, and it is new to the library: Civ. Code s1954.213 caps late fees on SUBMETERED WATER bills at $7 on the first bill and $10 on each subsequent bill, with all late fees in any 12-month period limited to 10 percent of the unpaid amount, and bars any late fee until 25 days after the bill is sent. Water charges are not rent (s1954.213(d)), so that cap does not touch a rent late fee - but a landlord who submeters has two different late-fee regimes running at once. See edu-water-submeter-billing-ca. SCOPE of the search: statutes only, exact phrases and the two word forms run; regulations, local ordinances and case law were not searched, and Orozco v. Casimiro and Del Monte Properties v. Dolan remain unread. | CA: 2026-09-29 (Addendum M.14): {{late_fee}} renamed {{late_fee_amount}}, the name clauseVariables.js resolves; the placeholder had always printed raw.

title: NSF Fee Limit
bodyText: If Tenant pays Rent or any other amount due under this Lease by check, draft or order for payment and it is not honored for lack of funds, because Tenant has no account with the drawee, or because Tenant stops payment, Tenant shall be liable to Landlord for the amount of the payment and a service charge of {{nsf_fee}}.
notes: CA: REWRITTEN 2026-09-19 against Civ. Code s1719(a) (primary text supplied by Taylor). Figures CONFIRMED - $25 first, $35 each subsequent 'to that payee' - but the prior dormant row carried three defects. (1) FRAMING: it said the cap applies 'as required by California law'. s1719(a)(1) is a statutory ENTITLEMENT capped at those amounts, not a requirement to charge. Third CA row found reciting a landlord option as a legal mandate, after month-to-month-notice-ca and the CO entry-notice precedent. (2) INSTRUMENT SCOPE - the substantive defect. The old row capped the fee for any 'dishonored or returned payment'. s1719(a)(6) defines the trigger as making, uttering, drawing or delivering a CHECK, DRAFT OR ORDER for the payment of money upon a bank or depository that refuses to honor it. A returned ACH debit or a declined card is not obviously an instrument drawn by the tenant, so s1719 may not reach electronic payment methods at all. That cuts both ways: the old row asserted a statutory safe harbour over payment types the statute may not cover, and for those types a returned-payment fee in a residential lease is an ordinary liquidated-damages provision governed by s1671(d) - VOID unless actual damages were impracticable or extremely difficult to fix. See late-fee-safe-harbor-ca; the two rows are now linked by that analysis. Clause scoped to checks, drafts and orders accordingly. (3) OMITTED EXCEPTIONS: s1719(a)(3) good-faith-dispute stop payment, where the payee recovers only on CLEAR AND CONVINCING evidence that no good faith dispute existed; (a)(4) written confirmation of financial institution error; (a)(5) written confirmation that the shortfall came from a delayed direct deposit of SOCIAL SECURITY OR GOVERNMENT BENEFIT ASSISTANCE. A flat fee clause misstates the law against benefit recipients in particular. All three now in body text. Note s1719(a)(6)(C): a STOP PAYMENT counts as passing a check on insufficient funds, subject to the good-faith-dispute carve-out. CROSS-CHAPTER: s1719 sits in Part 3, Obligations Imposed by Law - outside the landlord-tenant title. Instruction 7 pattern, fourth confirmation in CA. EXTEND SCREEN 2026-09-19: now supersedes the base row `returned-payments`, which is blocked for CA. s1719 NOW READ IN FULL 2026-09-19 - three additions. (1) TREBLE DAMAGES, s1719(a)(2): after a written demand by CERTIFIED MAIL stating the section's provisions, the check amount and the service charge, the drawer has 30 DAYS to pay; failing that, liability becomes the unpaid check amount PLUS TREBLE that amount, not less than $100 nor more than $1,500, in place of the service charge. (2) EXCEPTIONS to the service charge: a STOP PAYMENT in a good-faith dispute (payee must prove no good-faith dispute by clear and convincing evidence, s1719(a)(3), (b)); written confirmation of BANK ERROR (a)(4); and a delayed SOCIAL SECURITY or government benefit deposit (a)(5). For a stop payment, the demand must be in the prescribed s1719(c) form, sent certified with a receipt in evidence (d), and the payee must show a reasonable effort to reconcile before suing (e). s1719(j)(2): liability arises only ONCE per check. (3) NO POSTDATED-CHECK EXCLUSION anywhere in s1719 - candidate 427.4's North Dakota trap does not exist here. The ACH/card scope caveat stands: every limb is framed around a 'check, draft, or order'. | CA: SCRUB 2026-09-29 (checklist instruction 66, three-bucket test): kept the landlord's fee; the restated $25/$35 cap and the tenant's statutory defenses moved to edu-nsf-treble-damages-ca.

title: Returned Payments
bodyText: If any payment Tenant makes under this Lease by check, draft, order of payment, debit card order, or electronic funds transfer is refused by the drawee because of lack of funds, lack of credit, or lack of an account, or if Tenant stops payment on it with intent to defraud, Tenant will pay Landlord the bank fees Landlord actually incurred in tendering the payment, plus a service charge of $25 if the face value does not exceed $50, $30 if the face value exceeds $50 but does not exceed $300, or $40 if the face value exceeds $300, or 5 percent of the face value, whichever is greater. Landlord may require that the payment be replaced by a cashier's check, certified check, or money order. If more than two of Tenant's payments during the Term are returned, Landlord may require all future payments of Rent to be made by cashier's check, certified check, or money order. This Section does not limit any other remedy Florida law gives Landlord for a dishonored payment.
notes: FL: DORMANT ROW REWRITTEN AND ACTIVATED 2026-09-26 (instruction 21). Primary text pasted by Taylor 2026-09-26 from flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2026 (official 2026 Florida Statutes), read section-open with history lines. Supersedes returned-payments (base not tagged FL: the rewritten row states the measure the base's 'maximum amount permitted by applicable law' points to, and both cannot display). Controlling text: Fla. Stat. §68.065(2) (s. 1, ch. 2013-113 latest): 'In lieu of a service charge authorized under subsection (3), s. 832.062(4)(a), or s. 832.07, the payee ... may lawfully collect bank fees actually incurred ... plus a service charge of $25 ... $30 ... $40 ...; or 5 percent of the face value ..., whichever is greater.' What the pre-rigor row got right: the $25/$30/$40 tiers and the $50/$300 break points. What it got wrong: (1) the 5% alternative applies at EVERY tier, not only above $300; (2) actual bank fees are recoverable IN ADDITION; (3) the statute covers drafts, orders of payment, debit card orders and electronic funds transfers, not only checks (§68.065(1)); (4) it reaches stop-payments only with intent to defraud. The tiers also appear in §832.08(5), the state attorney's diversion-fee schedule, which is not a landlord cap. Additional remedy: after a 30-day written demand in the §68.065(4) form, treble damages (minimum $50) plus costs and fees in a civil action (§68.065(3)); hardship waiver (7) (edu-dishonored-payment-remedies-fl). The charge is not designated rent (library default), so it cannot be demanded in a §83.56(3) 3-day notice as rent. Replacement-method sentences carried from the base; no Florida payment-method statute in Part II (acceptable-payment-methods tagged FL).

title: Bounced Checks and Returned Payments
bodyText: Pennsylvania has no civil statute capping the fee a landlord may charge for a returned rent payment; a fee in the lease should be reasonable. Writing a check knowing it will not be paid is a crime. On conviction, the court orders repayment of the check, interest and a service charge of up to $50 (or the payee's actual bank fees if higher), but only if a written notice of the service charge was conspicuously displayed at the payee's premises when the check was given. After a conviction and a written demand at least 10 days before suit, the payee may sue for the greater of $100 or three times the check, limited to $500 more than the check's value.
notes: PA: Read section-open 2026-09-29 in the built-in browser on the General Assembly's official site (palegis.us) and, for court rules and regulations, the official Pennsylvania Code site (pacodeandbulletin.gov): The Landlord and Tenant Act of 1951 (1951 P.L. 69, No. 20) read whole from the official unconsolidated-statute text with every amendment note (newest: Act 88 of 2024, 2024 P.L. 944); the Pennsylvania Constitution and all 74 titles of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes (75 files) loaded from the official title files (29.28 million characters; revision stamps 2022-03-07 to 2026-09-16) and searched whole; all 262 acts of 2024, 2025 and 2026 screened in full text for landlord-tenant terms; no special-session act in 2024-2026 (PA log §1). P.S. numbers are Purdon's, which the official site does not print; each 1951-Act cite gives the Act section in parentheses (kickoff rule). DORMANT ROW REWRITTEN AND ACTIVATED (instruction 21). Former text (pre-project, UNVERIFIED, inactive): 'Any fee charged for a dishonored or returned payment under this Lease will not exceed $50.00, or the actual fee Landlord's bank charges if higher, as required by Pennsylvania law.' WHAT IT TURNED OUT TO BE: the $50-or-bank-fee figure is real but is CRIMINAL RESTITUTION on conviction under 18 Pa.C.S. § 4105(e)(3) (last amended Act 70 of 2007), conditioned on a written notice of the service charge 'conspicuously displayed on the payee's premises when the check was issued'; it is not a cap on lease fees and 'as required by Pennsylvania law' was wrong. The kickoff's candidate '13 Pa.C.S. § 3506' does not exist (Title 13 Chapter 35 ends at 13 Pa.C.S. § 3505; official Title 13 text, revised 2025-12-01). Civil damages after conviction: 42 Pa.C.S. § 8304 (greater of $100 or triple; not more than $500 over the check; 10-day written demand; partial restitution limit). ABSENCE: no civil returned-check fee cap located - Pa.C.S. regex '(returned|dishonou?red|bad|worthless) (check|instrument|payment)' near fee/charge: 18 Pa.C.S. § 4105, 7 Pa.C.S. § 6122 (mortgage licensees), 75 Pa.C.S. § 1374 only (PA log §17 search 80); unconsolidated "dishonored check" 18 results (banking, vehicle and 2008 Act 117 sections, none landlord). Converted from a lease clause to education because no statute constrains a lease fee; `returned-payments` (tagged PA, 'not to exceed the maximum amount permitted by applicable law') carries the lease term. Id kept so the dormant row is resolved in place.

notes: TX: DORMANT ROW REWRITTEN AND ACTIVATED 2026-09-25 (instruction 21). Primary text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-25 from the official Texas Constitution and Statutes site (statutes.capitol.texas.gov), with per-section history lines; read section-open. Controlling text: Tex. Bus. & Com. Code s3.506 (Added 2001; last Amended by Acts 2019, 86th Leg., R.S., Ch. 1352 (S.B. 346), eff. Jan. 1, 2020). Not in Tex. Prop. Code ch. 92. Pre-rigor row: the $30 figure was right. Its claim that the fee applies 'in addition to any fee the bank itself assesses' is NOT supported by s3.506(b), which sets a 'maximum processing fee of $30'. s3.506(e) says the section does not affect rights under a written contract - whether that lets a lease add the landlord's own bank charges on top is an AMBIGUITY (research-mode candidate, TX log s11.4); the clause stays inside $30 total. Requiring certified funds after dishonor is a written-lease payment requirement consistent with s92.011(a). | Prior (pre-rigor) body: Any processing fee charged for a dishonored or returned payment under this Lease will not exceed $30.00, in addition to any fee the bank itself assesses, as required by Texas law. | Earlier 2026-09-25 hold note: TX 2026-09-25: STILL DORMANT - research question pending Tex. title: Use of Security Deposit
bodyText: Tenant shall pay Landlord a security deposit of {{security_deposit}} (Security Deposit) prior to occupancy. Landlord may apply the Security Deposit to remedy a Tenant default under this Lease, including past due Rent, and to repair damage to the property caused by Tenant or Tenant's guests beyond ordinary wear and tear. Landlord will not apply the Security Deposit to normal wear and tear or to any damage or defective condition that preexisted the tenancy. Landlord may apply the Security Deposit to cleaning costs only if the property is substantially less clean at the end of the Term than it was at the start of the Term. The Security Deposit will not relieve Tenant of any obligation to pay Rent due under this Lease prior to its termination.
notes: CO added - verified this session (statute walk + full-library audit; content itself EDITED this session | NE extended (session 6, closing the last open NE item): Neb. Rev. Stat. §76-1416(2) permits applying the deposit 'to the payment of rent and the amount of damages which the landlord has suffered by reason of the tenant's noncompliance with the rental agreement or section 76-1421' — substantively the same rent-plus-damages-beyond-wear-and-tear framing this clause already uses. No last-month's-rent restriction like Kansas's, so no override needed. Not extended to WY in this pass — WY currently has no clause of this type at all (security-deposit-use-wy doesn't exist), a separate, pre-existing gap noticed while resolving this, not fixed here since it's outside this session's Nebraska-specific scope. | MN extended (Minnesota session, whole-library audit): matches Minn. Stat. § 504B.178, subd. 3(b) — landlord may withhold only for rent defaults and to restore the property, ordinary wear and tear excepted. No conflict. | ND extended (North Dakota session 1, statute walk): N.D.C.C. § 47-16-07.1(3) permits application to pet/negligence damage, unpaid rent, and cleaning/repair costs necessary to restore the property, reasonable wear and tear excepted — compatible with this clause's existing self-limiting language. No ND-specific override needed. | SD extended (South Dakota session 1, whole-library generic-clause audit): SDCL 43-32-6.1's deposit-application concept (deposit secures performance of the rental agreement) is compatible with the generic's existing self-limiting language (default/damage beyond wear-and-tear, not preexisting conditions); no SD-specific override needed for the use/application language itself. Return mechanics are SD-specific and handled separately by security-deposit-return-sd (switched off 2026-09-29). | WY ADDED 2026-08-28 (deposit split, Taylor's decision): WY previously folded application language into security-deposit-return-wy. Split to the CO pattern. Compatible with Wyo. Stat. 1-21-1208(a). TWO DELIBERATE GIVEAWAYS accepted: (1) cleaning deductions only if 'substantially less clean', vs 1208(a)'s 'clean to the condition at start'; (2) 1208(a)'s catch-all 'any other costs this Lease provides for' not carried over. Both more tenant-favorable than WY requires. | NV: Read in full 2026-09-24 against NRS 118A (revisor text Rev. 4/15/2026, 2025 session incorporated). Applies as written; narrower than 118A.242(4), which allows reasonable cleaning costs (clause limits cleaning deductions further - lawful, tenant-favourable). Return mechanics in security-deposit-return-nv. | TX: Read in full 2026-09-25 against Tex. Prop. Code ch. 92 (full chapter, section-open; Justia 2025 host copy with per-section history lines). Applies as written. Consistent with s92.104(a)-(b) (deductions for damages/charges the tenant is legally liable for; none for normal wear and tear as defined s92.001(4)). The cleaning limit is stricter than Texas requires - a voluntary landlord limit, lawful. | FL: Applies as written (tag-first screen, instruction 26). Fla. Stat. §83.49 does not bar applying the deposit during the tenancy (contrast NJ 46:8-21.1); §83.43(14) defines security deposits as money held 'as security for the performance of the rental agreement'. Return mechanics sit in security-deposit-return-fl (instruction 24 family). A pet deposit is 'deposit money' (§83.43(4)). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | AZ: Applies as written. A.R.S. §33-1321(D) lets the landlord apply prepaid rent and security to all rent and, subject to the duty to mitigate, to all charges specified in the signed lease or the Act, including damages from the tenant's noncompliance with §33-1341. This clause is narrower (no wear and tear, cleaning only if substantially less clean), which is a landlord choice, not a conflict. §33-1310(15): a reasonable charge for redecorating or cleaning is not "security". Return mechanics: security-deposit-return-az. s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | GA: Applies as written. O.C.G.A. § 44-7-34(a) allows retention for unpaid rent and late fees, abandonment, unpaid utilities, repair or cleaning contracted by the tenant with third parties, unpaid pet fees and actual damages from breach (with mitigation), and bars retention for ordinary wear and tear; this clause is narrower on cleaning, which is lawful. 'Prior to occupancy' works with O.C.G.A. § 44-7-33(a) only if the move-in damage list is presented BEFORE the deposit is tendered (`move-in-damage-list-ga`). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | SC: Tagged. Withholding is limited to accrued rent and damages from the tenant's noncompliance with S.C. Code Ann. § 27-40-510, which includes complying with the lease (S.C. Code Ann. § 27-40-510(8)), so 'remedy a Tenant default' and the cleaning sentence fit (S.C. Code Ann. § 27-40-410(a)). Deposit is held in trust (S.C. Code Ann. § 27-40-210(18)). | TN: Tagged 2026-09-28 (section text read 2026-09-28 in the built-in browser (Justia host copy of the 2025 Tennessee Code with history lines; 2025-2026 public chapters screened; TN log §1)). Consistent with the Act-county definition of a security deposit (Tenn. Code Ann. § 66-28-104(14): damage beyond ordinary wear and tear and monetary damage from breach) and § 66-28-301(e) (application to unpaid rent); the cleaning limit is more protective than the statute. No deposit statute outside Act counties. TN-SCOPE: STATEWIDE. | VA: Tagged 2026-09-28. VA-SCOPE: STATEWIDE. Read against the official Code of Virginia section-open (law.lis.virginia.gov; VA log §1). Basis: Consistent with Va. Code Ann. § 55.1-1226(A) (four permitted uses; the clause's limits on wear and tear, pre-existing damage and cleaning are narrower than (iii) 'other damages or charges as provided in the rental agreement' and lawful). Cap, timing and procedure are in security-deposit-return-va. | AL: Tagged. At termination the deposit may be applied only to accrued rent and to damages from the tenant's noncompliance with Ala. Code § 35-9A-301, itemized in writing (Ala. Code § 35-9A-201(b)); 'rent' includes all payments due under the lease (Ala. Code § 35-9A-141(12)). The clause's wear-and-tear, pre-existing-condition and cleaning limits are narrower than the statute, not broader. Return mechanics: `security-deposit-return-al`; cap: `security-deposit-cap-al`. s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | PA: Tagged. Consistent with 68 P.S. § 250.512(a) (Act § 512: damages caused by the tenant; withholding for nonpayment of rent or breach of any other lease condition); narrower on wear and tear and cleaning, so lawful. Return: `security-deposit-return-pa`. s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | UT: Utah Code Ann. § 57-17-3(1) allows applying a deposit to rent, damage beyond reasonable wear and tear, other costs and fees provided for in the contract, and cleaning; this clause is narrower (cleaning only if substantially less clean), which the landlord may choose. s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | IL: Tagged. Withholding for damage beyond normal wear and tear requires the itemized statement (765 ILCS 710/1(a)); security-deposit-return-il and deposit-cost-schedule-il supply the Illinois mechanics. Read section-open 2026-09-30 (IL log §1). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | ID: Idaho Code § 6-321(1): a deposit is refunded 'except amounts necessary to cover the contingencies specified in the deposit arrangement', and may not be kept for normal wear and tear. This clause is the specification of contingencies; it names default, past-due Rent, damage beyond ordinary wear and tear and cleaning. Lawful as written. Read section-open 2026-09-30 from legislature.idaho.gov (ID log s1). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed. | OK: Okla. Stat. tit. 41, § 115(B): the deposit may be applied to accrued rent and damages from the tenant's noncompliance with the act and the rental agreement; the clause's 'remedy a Tenant default' and wear-and-tear limits fit. Okla. Stat. tit. 41, § 115(F): unless the rental agreement provides otherwise the tenant may not apply the deposit to the last month's rent; the clause's last sentence keeps that default. Return, demand and the six-month reversion: security-deposit-return-ok; escrow: edu-security-deposit-rules-ok. Read section-open 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-01 from oklegislature.gov (OK log §1). s5a.1: states-only change, no propagation owed.
