title: Late Fee
bodyText: If Tenant fails to pay Monthly Rent in full within {{late_fee_grace_days}} days after it is due, a late fee of {{late_fee_amount}} will be assessed. Acceptance of a late payment does not waive Landlord's right to require full payment of Rent on the date it is due or to pursue any other remedy available under this Lease.
notes: NV: Section-open read of revisor text (leg.state.nv.us, Rev. 4/15/2026). NRS 118A.210(4) (A. 2019, 2021): reasonable late fee as set forth in the rental agreement; in a tenancy longer than week to week no late fee until at least 3 calendar days after due; must not exceed 5% of periodic rent; maximum must not be increased based on a previously imposed late fee. Builder constraints: {{late_fee_grace_days}} >= 3; {{late_fee_amount}} <= 5% of {{monthly_rent}} (the all-in figure, 118A.125/.200(6)). 118A.150: rent includes reasonable and actual late fees in the agreement. 118A.355(1)(d)/.380(1)(c): withholding tenants incur no late fee. Waiver-by-acceptance sentence kept from base; no NV waiver statute located in 118A (Ch. 40 not read). Supersedes late-fee for NV rather than tagging it: base states no cap and NV's three limits are hard statutory numbers. | NV: SCRUB 2026-09-29 (checklist instruction 66, three-bucket test): kept the landlord's fee and grace period (the lease must state them); the 3-day floor and 5% cap are now bracket prompts for the landlord, and the rules moved to edu-late-fee-rules-nv. | NV: SCRUB 2026-09-29 (checklist instruction 66, three-bucket test): follow-up fix: removed the two limit brackets placed next to {{variables}}, which would have printed in the lease because nothing prompts the landlord to edit a clause whose blanks fill automatically; the limits stay in edu-late-fee-rules-nv and the builder check (Addendum M.13).

title: Surety Bond Option
bodyText: Tenant may, if Landlord consents, purchase a surety bond in place of all or part of the Security Deposit.
notes: NV: Section-open read of revisor text (leg.state.nv.us, Rev. 4/15/2026). NRS 118A.242(1)-(3); 118A.240(1)-(2) (A. 2021). "Security deposit" = any payment, deposit, fee or charge used to remedy rent default, repair non-normal-wear damage, or clean - so pet and cleaning deposits count toward the cap; excludes an option-to-purchase payment and a surety-bond premium. 118A.242(5): tenant may dispute an itemized accounting to the surety within 30 days; surety may not credit-report absent judgment. Does NOT supersede security-deposit-use (CA's cap row did; that would strip NV of the use clause). Builder constraint: sum of deposit fields <= 3 x {{monthly_rent}}. | NV: SCRUB 2026-09-29 (checklist instruction 66, three-bucket test): kept the surety-bond option (the landlord's choice to accept one); the three-month cap and the bar on requiring a bond are in edu-security-deposit-rules-nv.

title: Security Deposit Return
bodyText: Except for a nonrefundable cleaning charge of [state a reasonable amount, or 'none'], no part of the Security Deposit is nonrefundable. Tenant is asked to give Landlord a forwarding address in writing.
notes: NV: Section-open read of revisor text (leg.state.nv.us, Rev. 4/15/2026). NRS 118A.242(4), (6)-(9) (A. 2021). Deadline: 30 days after termination of tenancy (no forwarding-address trigger; clause only ASKS for one). Delivery: personally at place rent is paid, or mail to present/last known address. Penalty 118A.242(6)-(7): liable for the entire deposit plus up to the amount of the entire deposit, court weighing good faith, course of conduct and harm. (8): only a reasonable nonrefundable CLEANING charge may be carved out; any waiver/modification of s242 rights void. (9): tenant's claim has priority over landlord's creditors. 118A.350(3)/.355(3)/.370(1)/.390(3)/.400(2): deposit returnable on those terminations; 118A.345(5): no withholding for DV early termination. INSTRUCTION 24 FAMILY: closes NV's gap in the security-deposit-return REQUIRED family. | NV: SCRUB 2026-09-29 (checklist instruction 66, three-bucket test): kept the landlord's nonrefundable cleaning charge (it must be stated in the lease) and the forwarding-address request; the claim, accounting and return rules are in edu-security-deposit-rules-nv.

title: Move-In Inventory and Condition Record
bodyText: Landlord and Tenant have completed and signed a written record of the inventory and condition of the premises under Tenant's exclusive custody and control. That signed record is attached to and forms part of this Lease.
notes: NV: Section-open read of revisor text (leg.state.nv.us, Rev. 4/15/2026). NRS 118A.200(3)(k): any written rental agreement MUST contain "a signed record of the inventory and condition of the premises under the exclusive custody and control of the tenant." Unlike K.S.A. 58-2548 (joint, within 5 days after start) NV sets no window - the record is lease content, so it must exist at execution. Why not massage move-in-inventory-ks: its 5-day post-start window is Kansas statute and would put the NV record outside the executed agreement. BUILDER: signed attachment needed before the lease is final.

title: Manager, Agent and Owner Disclosure
bodyText: Persons authorized to manage the premises: {{manager_name}}, {{manager_address}}. Person within the state authorized to act for Landlord for service of process and for receiving notices and demands: {{owner_agent_name}}, {{owner_agent_address}}. Principal or corporate owner: {{owner_name}}, {{owner_address}}. Emergency telephone number of a responsible person who resides in the county, or within 60 miles, where the premises are located: {{emergency_phone}}. Landlord will keep this information current.
notes: NV: Section-open read of revisor text (leg.state.nv.us, Rev. 4/15/2026). NRS 118A.260(1)-(2) (A. 2007): in writing at or before commencement; agent for process must be WITHIN THE STATE; emergency contact must reside in the county or within 60 miles. 118A.260(3)-(5): a party who signs for the landlord without complying becomes the landlord's agent for process and obligations; undisclosed landlord remains liable. 118A.270: alternative - posted notices (every elevator plus one conspicuous place, or two conspicuous places). 118A.410: after tenant demand, actual damages or $25, whichever greater. Separate from landlord-identity-oh / -ks / -ne / -mn because none carries the in-state agent or 60-mile emergency contact.

title: Delay in Delivering Possession
bodyText: If Landlord fails to deliver possession of the property to Tenant as required by this Lease, Rent abates until possession is delivered, and Tenant may: (a) terminate this Lease on at least 5 days' written notice to Landlord, in which case Landlord will return all prepaid Rent, the Security Deposit to the extent recoverable by Tenant, and any payment, deposit, fee or charge made to secure the execution of this Lease; (b) demand performance of this Lease and, if Tenant elects, bring an action for possession against Landlord or any person wrongfully in possession and recover actual damages, except that Landlord is not liable for damages if Landlord exercised due diligence to evict a holdover tenant or remedy the condition keeping Tenant from taking possession; or (c) pursue any other remedy available to Tenant, including recovery of actual damages.
notes: NV: Section-open read of revisor text (leg.state.nv.us, Rev. 4/15/2026). NRS 118A.370 (A. 2021). Base possession-delay conflicts: it keeps the lease "in full force" and allows termination only after 30 days, while 118A.370(1) lets the tenant terminate on 5 days' notice at any time possession is not delivered - and 118A.220(1)(a) voids a waiver of chapter rights. possession-delay-ks/-ne are close but carry KS 1.5x / NE 3x willful-failure penalties NV lacks, so they cannot be shared. 118A.280: duty to deliver at commencement in habitable condition. | NV: SCRUB 2026-09-29 (checklist instruction 66, three-bucket test): switched off, not deleted. It restates a tenant right or landlord duty that applies whatever the lease says, so the content moved to education (edu-possession-delay-nv). Kept for a possible comprehensive-lease option.

title: Tenant Maintenance Obligations
bodyText: Tenant will: keep the part of the premises Tenant occupies and uses as clean and safe as the condition of the premises permits; dispose of all ashes, garbage, rubbish and other waste from the dwelling unit in a clean and safe manner; keep all plumbing fixtures in the dwelling unit as clean as their condition permits; use all electrical, plumbing, sanitary, heating, ventilating, air-conditioning and other facilities and appliances, including elevators, in a reasonable manner; not deliberately or negligently render the premises uninhabitable or destroy, deface, damage, impair or remove any part of the premises, or knowingly permit any person to do so; and conduct himself or herself, and require other persons on the premises with Tenant's consent to conduct themselves, in a manner that will not disturb a neighbor's peaceful enjoyment of the premises. Tenant will pay for repairs, maintenance or other work needed because of a condition caused by the deliberate or negligent act or omission of Tenant, a member of Tenant's household, or another person on the premises with Tenant's consent.
notes: NV: Section-open read of revisor text (leg.state.nv.us, Rev. 4/15/2026). NRS 118A.310(1)(b)-(g) near-verbatim; last sentence from 118A.290(5) (A. 2023). Supersedes base tenant-maintenance for NV: the base's "maintain the property in the same condition as it was delivered" imposes a repair duty regardless of fault, which collides with 118A.290(4) (no fee or charge for repairs that are the landlord's duty, including home-warranty deductibles/copays, 2023) and 118A.220(1)(a). Same structure as CA's override (tenant-maintenance-obligations-ca, s1941.2); KS/NE/ND tenant-duties rows carry their own statutes' code-compliance limb that 118A.310 lacks.

title: Pet Policy
bodyText: Tenant may keep only pets identified in writing to and approved by Landlord: [list approved pets, or state that no pets are permitted]. Any pet deposit is part of the Security Deposit, is refundable as provided in this Lease, and counts toward the limit on total security. Any monthly pet fee is a mandatory fee included in the Monthly Rent stated in this Lease and is not charged in addition to it. Tenant is responsible for all damage, waste removal, odor, and disturbance caused by a pet. Landlord may revoke approval of a pet that becomes a nuisance or safety concern. Landlord may enter the property in connection with a pet only as permitted by this Lease's Access & Entry terms and applicable law, including without notice in an emergency. This Section does not apply to an assistance animal.
notes: NV: Section-open read of revisor text (leg.state.nv.us, Rev. 4/15/2026). Every existing pet-policy row fails NV somewhere: base/-sd indemnity reaches the landlord's own negligence (118A.220(1)(d)); base/-ne "without liability" exculpation; base/-ks/-ne non-emergency entry to remove a pet is not an access purpose 118A.330 allows ((4): no other right of access); and every row prices pet rent OUTSIDE the rent figure, which 118A.200(6) (2025) forbids for a mandatory fee. 118A.200(3)(c): lease must address occupancy by pets. 118A.240: pet deposit = security deposit (cap 118A.242(1)). 118A.320(1)(g): a later rule may not take away a pet right before the agreement ends. Assistance-animal carve-out deliberately generic - NRS 118.105 not yet read (see log). | NV (text batch 2, 2026-09-24): NRS 118.105 now read (host): the assistance-animal carve-out stands; state law covers animals that "assist, support or provide service".

title: Payment Methods
bodyText: Rent and other amounts due under this Lease may be paid by the following methods: [list accepted payment methods]. At least one listed method does not require Tenant to pay any fee or charge for using it or to provide information about a bank account of Tenant (payment by a check that contains such information is permitted). If Tenant may pay through an Internet website or online portal, the fee Landlord charges Tenant for using it is [state amount, or "none"], which does not exceed the fee charged by the operator of the website or portal. Landlord may change the accepted methods on reasonable written notice, but will always keep at least one method that meets the requirements of this Section.
notes: NV: Section-open read of revisor text (leg.state.nv.us, Rev. 4/15/2026). NRS 118A.303 (2025, Stats. p. 1412). (1): at least one method with no fee AND no bank-account information (check exception). (2): portal fee capped at operator's fee AND must be separately identified in any written rental agreement. Supersedes acceptable-payment-methods for NV (as payment-methods-ca does for CA). CONSOLIDATION CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: writing the fee-free-method promise into the base would impose a new obligation on landlords in eight states that do not require it (a product change, not a uniform clarification); a vague "if law requires" hedge would leave the NV portal-fee disclosure unmet. effective_from left blank: the session-law effective-date sections were not read.  | NV (text batch 2, 2026-09-24): effective_from 2025-10-01: AB 121 (2025) enrolled text read on the Legislature archive - it contains NO effective-date section, so the Oct. 1 default applies (NRS 218D.330, not itself read; corroborated by the NELIS chapter note "Chapter 227, effective October 1, 2025" as reported by BillTrack50).  | NV (research pass, 2026-09-24): Research pass on 118A.303(1)(a): unresolved (see returned-payments-nv). Safe product default: a fee-free way to pay by personal check (in person or by mail) should always be among the listed methods; do not rely on money orders or cashier's checks as the only compliant method.

title: Returned Payments
bodyText: If any payment of Rent is returned for insufficient funds or otherwise fails, Tenant will pay a returned-payment charge of [state amount; $25 or less], not to exceed the maximum amount permitted by applicable law. Landlord may then require that the payment be replaced by a cashier's check, certified check, money order, or another payment method that does not require Tenant to pay a fee or provide bank account information. If more than two of Tenant's payments during the Term are returned for insufficient funds, Landlord may require all future payments to be made by those methods. Landlord will continue to accept at least one method of payment that does not require Tenant to pay a fee or provide bank account information.
notes: NV: Section-open read of revisor text (leg.state.nv.us, Rev. 4/15/2026). Supersedes returned-payments for NV. Two NV conflicts in the base: (1) 118A.200(3)(g) requires the lease to state charges for return of a dishonored check - base leaves the amount unstated; (2) restricting a tenant to cashier's/certified check/money order - each normally carrying an issuer fee, and certified checks a bank account - risks removing the fee-free, no-bank-information method 118A.303(1) requires. AMBIGUITY FLAGGED (research-mode trigger: ambiguous statute language): whether an issuer's fee is a "fee or charge for using the method" under 118A.303(1)(a); the clause is drafted to be lawful on either reading. OPEN: NV dishonored-check charge cap is outside 118A and not yet located; clause defers to it. | NV (research pass, 2026-09-24): Research pass: NRS 597.960 caps a seller's dishonored-check fee at $25 for goods or services (reach to rent unsettled) - the bracket now steers to $25 or less as the safe figure. NRS 41.620 civil remedy described in edu-returned-check-remedies-nv. Money-order question (118A.303(1)(a)) UNRESOLVED: no appellate authority or official guidance; landlord-side counsel (Karsaz Law, 2025-10-01) calls "landlord-imposed fees only" the prevailing reading, while Legal Aid Center of Southern Nevada material lists "a check or money order" as a free method - a conflict between secondary sources. The clause stays drafted to be lawful on either reading. Karsaz also reports courts adding a 118A.303-noncompliance checkbox to the Tenant Affidavit form - i.e. it is being raised as an eviction defense.

title: Rent During the Term
bodyText: During the Term, the Monthly Rent will not be increased except as this Lease expressly provides.
notes: NV: Section-open read of revisor text (leg.state.nv.us, Rev. 4/15/2026). NRS 118A.300 (A. 1983, 2021). 60 days; 30 for periodic tenancy < 1 month. No frequency or amount cap located in 118A. 118A.510 (retaliatory rent increase) text not yet read in official form. Rent-control preemption: not checked (outside 118A). | NV (text batch 2, 2026-09-24): NRS 118A.510 now read: a rent increase in retaliation for protected activity is barred, but an increase applied uniformly to all tenants is excepted (510(3)(d)). | NV: SCRUB 2026-09-29 (checklist instruction 66, three-bucket test): kept the no-mid-term-increase term; the statutory 60-day and 30-day notice rule moved to edu-rent-increase-notice-nv.

title: Fire or Casualty: Landlord's Right to End the Lease
bodyText: If the property is damaged or destroyed by fire or casualty to an extent that Tenant's enjoyment of it is substantially impaired, Landlord may terminate this Lease.
notes: NV: Section-open read of revisor text (leg.state.nv.us, Rev. 4/15/2026). NRS 118A.400 (A. 2021). Same URLTA architecture as fire-casualty-termination-ks but the tenant's notice window is 7 days (KS 5) and NV expressly gives the LANDLORD a termination right - cannot share the KS row. | NV: SCRUB 2026-09-29 (checklist instruction 66, three-bucket test): kept the landlord's termination right; the tenant's statutory options moved to edu-casualty-termination-nv.

title: Property Left After Tenancy
bodyText: If Tenant abandons the property or leaves personal property on it after an eviction or the end of the rental period, Landlord will reasonably provide for the safe storage of that property for 30 days and may charge the reasonable and actual costs of inventory, moving and storage before releasing it to Tenant or Tenant's authorized representative within that period. After the 30-day period, Landlord may dispose of the property and recover reasonable costs out of the property or its value, but only after making reasonable efforts to locate Tenant, mailing Tenant written notice of the intention to dispose of it (to Tenant's present address or, if unknown, last known address), and waiting 14 days after that notice. Vehicles will be handled as the law provides for abandoned vehicles. For 5 days after any eviction or lockout, Landlord will give Tenant a reasonable opportunity to retrieve essential personal effects, including medication, baby formula, basic clothing and personal care items. In the absence of notice of abandonment, Tenant is presumed to have abandoned the property if absent for one-half of a rental period, unless Rent is current or Tenant has notified Landlord in writing of an intended absence.
notes: NV: Section-open read of revisor text (leg.state.nv.us, Rev. 4/15/2026). NRS 118A.460 (A. 1987, 1995, 2019) and 118A.450. Landlord liable only for negligent or wrongful acts in storage (118A.460(1)(a)) - not restated as an exculpation. Disputes over costs and essential-effects access go to the NRS 40.253 procedures (not read). Vehicles: NRS ch. 487 (not read). Topic parity with abandoned-property-wy/-ks/-mn/-nd/-sd; none shareable (different periods and value thresholds).

title: Termination for Domestic Violence, Harassment, Sexual Assault or Stalking
bodyText: If Tenant, a cotenant, or a household member (a person related by blood or marriage and actually residing with Tenant or a cotenant) is the victim of domestic violence, harassment, sexual assault or stalking, as those terms are defined by applicable law, Tenant or any cotenant may terminate this Lease by giving Landlord written notice, effective at the end of the current rental period or 30 days after the notice is provided, whichever occurs sooner. The notice must describe the reason for termination and be accompanied by: for domestic violence, a copy of an order for protection, a written law enforcement report showing the victim notified the agency of the domestic violence, or an affidavit in the form the law prescribes signed by a qualified third party; for harassment, sexual assault or stalking, a written law enforcement report or a copy of a temporary or extended protective order. This right applies only if the events occurred within the 90 days immediately before the notice. A terminating Tenant or cotenant is liable only for Rent owed through the date of termination and any other outstanding obligations; Landlord may keep prepaid Rent for the rental period in which this Lease terminates, refunding any amount exceeding what is owed for that period; and the Security Deposit will not be withheld because of the early termination. Landlord will not give the adverse party any information about the whereabouts of Tenant, a cotenant or a household member. After giving notice, Tenant, a cotenant or a household member may require Landlord to install a new lock at their cost, which Landlord may do by rekeying a lock in good working condition or replacing the locking mechanism with one of equal or superior quality; Landlord will not give the adverse party a key to the new lock, or access to the dwelling to reclaim property unless a law enforcement officer is present. Landlord will not disclose, describe or characterize a termination under this Section as an early termination to a prospective landlord.
notes: NV: Section-open read of revisor text (leg.state.nv.us, Rev. 4/15/2026). NRS 118A.345 (A. 2017) and 118A.347 (affidavit form). Household member is NARROW - blood or marriage and actually residing (118A.345(12)(e)) - stated in the clause (L.5). Incorporated definitions NOT read: NRS 33.018 (domestic violence), 200.366, 200.571, 200.575; the clause defers to them rather than paraphrasing scope. 118A.345(6): adverse party civilly liable to landlord for economic losses; (10) landlord's unrelated termination rights preserved. Retaliation protection 118A.510(1)(h) seen only in a host reproduction - not relied on. Qualified-third-party list in edu-dv-termination-documentation-nv. | NV: SCRUB 2026-09-29 (checklist instruction 66, three-bucket test): switched off, not deleted. It restates a tenant right or landlord duty that applies whatever the lease says, so the content moved to education (edu-dv-termination-documentation-nv). Kept for a possible comprehensive-lease option.

title: Termination for Relocation for Care or Death of a Cotenant
bodyText: Notwithstanding anything else in this Lease: (a) if a physical or mental condition of a Tenant who is 60 years of age or older or has a physical or mental disability requires that Tenant to relocate because of a need for care or treatment that cannot be provided in the dwelling, that Tenant may terminate this Lease by giving Landlord 30 days' written notice within 60 days after relocating, and a cotenant may do the same if the cotenant is 60 years of age or older or has a physical or mental disability, or became a tenant on or after the date the relocating Tenant signed; and (b) upon the death of the spouse or cotenant of a Tenant who is 60 years of age or older or has a physical or mental disability, that Tenant may terminate this Lease by giving Landlord 60 days' written notice within 3 months after the death. The notice must set forth the facts showing the right to terminate and, for a relocation, include reasonable verification of the condition and of the need to relocate for care or treatment. The death of a Tenant does not by itself give Landlord a right to terminate this Lease.
notes: NV: Section-open read of revisor text (leg.state.nv.us, Rev. 4/15/2026). NRS 118A.340 (A. 2005). Cotenant limb in (1)(b) reproduced with both alternatives. topic_key termination-infirmity (MN's 504B.266 row has different triggers and documentation - not shareable). | NV: SCRUB 2026-09-29 (checklist instruction 66, three-bucket test): switched off, not deleted. It restates a tenant right or landlord duty that applies whatever the lease says, so the content moved to education (edu-infirmity-death-termination-nv). Kept for a possible comprehensive-lease option.

title: Display of the United States Flag
bodyText: Landlord will not prohibit Tenant from displaying the flag of the United States within the portion of the premises Tenant has the right to occupy and use exclusively, where the flag is made of cloth, fabric or paper, is displayed from a pole or staff or in a window, and is displayed consistently with federal flag law. This right does not cover commercial advertising or a depiction of the flag made of balloons, flora, lights, paint, paving, roofing, siding or other building, decorative or landscaping components. Landlord may adopt rules that reasonably restrict the placement and manner of display. In any action to enforce this right, the prevailing party may recover reasonable attorney's fees and costs.
notes: NV: Section-open read of revisor text (leg.state.nv.us, Rev. 4/15/2026). NRS 118A.325 (2003) and 118A.200(3)(n): the lease MUST contain information about this right - hence REQUIRED. flag-display-oh not shared: Ohio protects four flags and adds a pole/bracket consultation duty; NV protects only the U.S. flag and allows placement/manner rules.

title: Display of Religious or Cultural Items
bodyText: This Lease does not prohibit Tenant from displaying religious or cultural items on the entry door or doorframe of the dwelling or otherwise in or on the dwelling, meaning items displayed or affixed because of sincerely held religious or cultural beliefs, practices or traditions. The right does not extend to a display that is larger than 36 by 12 inches or larger than the door on which or whose frame it is displayed; a display larger than 36 by 12 inches immediately adjacent or affixed to the entry; or a display that threatens public health, safety or welfare, hinders opening or closing an entry door, violates any law, promotes discriminatory behavior, or is obscene or otherwise illegal. Landlord may adopt policies that reasonably restrict placement and manner. If Landlord must work on the entry door or doorframe, Landlord will give at least 7 days' written notice except in an emergency, and may either require Tenant to remove the display temporarily or, if Tenant consents or does not respond within a reasonable period, remove it and store it respectfully; the display may be returned within 72 hours after the work is completed. In any action to enforce this right, the prevailing party may recover reasonable attorney's fees and costs.
notes: NV: Section-open read of revisor text (leg.state.nv.us, Rev. 4/15/2026). NRS 118A.327 (2025, Stats. p. 1989) and 118A.200(3)(o) (2025): lease MUST contain information about this right, and (1) says the rental agreement "must not" prohibit it. Size limit rendered from the statute's "36 by 12 square inches" as 36 by 12 inches - drafting ambiguity in the statute itself, flagged. NEW TOPIC. effective_from left blank: the session-law effective-date sections were not read.  | NV (text batch 2, 2026-09-24): effective_from 2025-07-01: SB 201 (2025) enrolled text read on the Legislature archive, Sec. 3 "This act becomes effective on July 1, 2025." UNCODIFIED Sec. 2: any contrary provision in a rental agreement or landlord policy in effect on July 1, 2025 is void; landlords had to amend policies by Oct. 1, 2025 and must remove void lease terms on or before renewal. The enrolled bill confirms the size limit is written "36 by 12 square inches" in the enacted text itself - the ambiguity is the Legislature's, not a reproduction error.

title: Nuisance Law Summary and Reporting Procedure
bodyText: Summary of the public nuisance law: A person commits a misdemeanor who commits or maintains a public nuisance (as defined by state law) for which no special punishment is prescribed, willfully omits or refuses to perform any legal duty relating to removal of such a nuisance, or lets or permits any building or portion of it to be used knowing it is intended to be or is being used for committing or maintaining such a nuisance. Reporting: Tenant may report a nuisance to [name and contact information of the local law enforcement or code enforcement agency], and may report a violation of a building, safety or health code or regulation to [name and contact information of the local building, code enforcement or health authority].
notes: NV: NRS 118A.200(3)(l)-(m): the lease MUST contain a summary of NRS 202.470 and information on how a tenant may report a nuisance and a code violation to the appropriate authorities. 118A.200(3) read section-open. NRS 202.470 NOT READ IN REVISOR TEXT: the official ch. 202 page truncated before it; wording above follows a host reproduction (Justia 2023, source line 1911 C&P s298; RL s6563; NCL s10246). NEEDS_REVIEW because the official ch. 202 index now titles 202.480 "Abatement of nuisance; civil penalty" where older reproductions say "Abatement of nuisance" - a 2025 change in the same subchapter, so 202.470's currency cannot be assumed (L.8). Agencies are local - municipal layer (Clark County/Las Vegas, Washoe County/Reno) flagged, not resolved. | NV (text batch 2, 2026-09-24): Text supplied by Taylor 2026-09-24 from the Justia 2025 NRS reproduction (host, with source lines) - one notch below revisor text, same basis CA accepted. NRS 202.470 now read with source line [1911 C&P s298; RL s6563; NCL s10246] - never amended. NEEDS_REVIEW CLEARED. MY CURRENCY FLAG WAS WRONG: I inferred a 2025 change to the subchapter from 202.480's longer revisor title; 202.480's source line shows its only amendment was 2009 (the "civil penalty" limb), and the shorter title I compared against was a host's abbreviated index, not an older official title. Also read: 202.450 (definition - body now points to it rather than paraphrasing), 202.460, 202.480 (court-ordered abatement plus $500-$5,000 civil penalty). 202.450(10): a tenant's request for emergency assistance under 118A.515 is not a public nuisance.

title: Single-Family Residence Occupancy Disclosure
bodyText: [Place at the top of the first page of the Lease, in a font size at least two times larger than any other font size in the Lease. Include only if the property is a single-family residence (a structure of not more than four units, other than a manufactured home) and this Lease is not signed by an authorized agent of Landlord who holds a permit to engage in property management:] NOTICE: State law contains rebuttable presumptions that a tenant does not have lawful occupancy of the dwelling unless the rental agreement (1) is notarized or is signed by an authorized agent of the landlord who holds a property management permit, and (2) includes the current address and telephone number of the landlord or the landlord's authorized representative. This agreement is valid and enforceable against the landlord and the tenant regardless of whether it is notarized or signed by such an agent, and regardless of whether it includes that address and telephone number.
notes: NV: Section-open read of revisor text (leg.state.nv.us, Rev. 4/15/2026). NRS 118A.200(4) and (10) (A. 2017, 2025). Content prescribed by (4)(a)-(b); NRS 205.0813 and 205.0817 (the presumptions themselves) NOT read - the disclosure only has to state what (4) lists, so the clause is verified against (4). SCHEMA GAP: first-page position and a relative font-size rule (2x the largest other font) - a harder layout requirement than CA's absolute type-size floors. NEW TOPIC. | NV (text batch 2, 2026-09-24): CORRECTION: this subsection was NOT changed in 2025 - both 2025 enrolled bills (AB 121, SB 201) reproduce it as existing text; it dates from the 2017 amendment in the section history. Context now read: NRS 40.412 (housebreaking/unlawful-occupancy lockout) uses the NRS 205.0813/.0817 definitions this disclosure refers to - the practical risk the disclosure guards against is a real tenant being treated as an unlawful occupant. 205.0813/.0817 themselves still unread.

title: Required Lease Contents and Copies
bodyText: A written rental agreement must be signed by you or your agent and the tenant or the tenant's agent, and you must give the tenant one copy free at signing and further copies within a reasonable time on request (a reasonable fee is allowed for extras). On request you must also give a prospective tenant a copy of the lease they would sign. Every written lease must address: duration; rent (as a single all-in figure) and how and when it is paid; occupancy by children or pets; services included; required fees and their purposes; required deposits and the conditions for refund; charges for late or partial payment and for a dishonored check; your inspection rights; who, or how many people, will occupy; who pays which utilities; a signed inventory and condition record; a summary of the state public-nuisance statute; how a tenant can report a nuisance or a code violation; and the tenant's rights to display the U.S. flag and religious or cultural items. Using a lease that does not conform is unlawful, and any nonconforming provision is void. With no written lease, the law presumes no restriction on children or pets, maintenance and trash service at no charge, no late or dishonored-check charges, and a return of the premises in move-in condition except normal wear.
notes: NV: Section-open read of revisor text (leg.state.nv.us, Rev. 4/15/2026). NRS 118A.200(1)-(3), (5), (9) and 118A.235 (2025). title: Application and Screening Fees
bodyText: If you collect an application, credit-report or background-check fee from an applicant and then rent the unit to someone else without actually doing the thing the fee paid for (processing the application, pulling the report), you must refund that fee. You may not charge an application, credit-report or background-check fee for a minor (under 18) who is a member of the applicant's household - household meaning people living together who are related by blood, adoption, marriage or domestic partnership. State law sets no cap on the amount of an application fee.
notes: NV: Section-open read of revisor text (leg.state.nv.us, Rev. 4/15/2026). NRS 118A.306 (2025, Stats. p. 1413). No cap on the amount of an application fee located in 118A. NEW TOPIC (fee refund + minor-fee ban); relates to the screening-fairness row. effective_from left blank: the session-law effective-date sections were not read.  | NV (text batch 2, 2026-09-24): effective_from 2025-10-01: AB 121 (2025) enrolled text read on the Legislature archive - it contains NO effective-date section, so the Oct. 1 default applies (NRS 218D.330, not itself read; corroborated by the NELIS chapter note "Chapter 227, effective October 1, 2025" as reported by BillTrack50). | NV (gap-discovery backfill, 2026-09-27): Cap: CONFIRMED ABSENT (statutes).
